1.
List has been revised.
2. Second supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Dinesh Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Deepak Kumar Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.208 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 328, 411 and 34 I.P.C., Police Station Sadar Bazar, District Meerut, during the pendency of trial.
Anil Kumar @ Warwa @ Rajinder Singh @ ... vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71440184/
1 5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant had deposited the amount of Rs.1.5 lakhs with the Trial Court and remaining Rs.50,000/- have also been deposited with the Trial Court.
The said receipt has been filed with the second supplementary affidavit filed today.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant has complied with the conditions as such he is entitled for bail.
The applicant is languishing in jail as he could not be enlarged on bail in the case of Gangsters Act and in another case.
He has to apply for bail in the said two cases.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 10.12.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed much reliance upon the judgment of Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of U.P. And Another, 2020 (11) SCC 648, wherein the Apex Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail, if otherwise his case for bail is made out.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of U.P. And Another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the fact that the applicant has complied with the order of this Court dated 02.11.2023, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Anil Kumar @ Warwa @ Rajinder Singh @ Shyam Singh @ Sem Alvish Dimalo,
who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

entities.text: Anil Kumar @ Warwa @ Rajinder Singh @ Shyam Singh @ Sem Alvish Dimalo
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
